trust_decision.summary: The username field of the auth cookie (HMAC-checked with AUTH_KEY, not escaped) is trusted as a SQL string literal in User_Model::getUserDataByLogin, which is called from LoginAuth::validateAuthCookie.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'via Authentication Cookie', so an engineer starts at validateAuthCookie, which splits the cookie and passes the username on to the model.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any request that carries the AUTH_COOKIE_NAME cookie (or POST field): admin/* via LoginAuth::isLogin/checkLogin, and the front-end api_controller auth() -> checkAuthCookie. Also POST admin/account.php?action=dosignin (user field) via LoginAuth::checkUser.
fix_sites.module_kind: model (data-access layer, one level below the auth library)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Cookie forgery needs AUTH_KEY, because the username is HMAC-bound at include/lib/loginauth.php:132-137. A solver could argue the input is already authenticated and leave the model alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Login passes the username already addslashes()-ed by Input::postStrVar into the same getUserDataByLogin, so escaping it again (the published fix) double-escapes. A user name containing a quote or backslash would then stop matching at login and in cookies set from the escaped name. An over-broad fix such as rejecting all non-alphanumeric account values would also break email login on the fallback query.

O6_input_shapes: plain string username taken from the first '|'-separated cookie element
same function reached with an email (second query, include/model/user_model.php:98)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: isUserExist/isNicknameExist/isMailExist interpolate their argument raw, and every caller at the pinned commit escapes it upstream through Input::*StrVar. A new caller that passes a cookie- or session-derived value would be a realistic sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The model layer has no escaping convention at all and relies on its callers, so a maintainer adding, say, a 'remember me' lookup by email would plausibly skip it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: updateUserByMail takes $mail from $_SESSION['mail'] (admin/account.php:278-279), a value that crosses a session boundary. If that session value were ever set from unescaped input, this would be a how-type save/reload sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Session-stored values look trusted to a reviewer, and the escaping happens only where the value is first written.

O9_family: CWE-89 SQL injection (string literal in a hand-built query, data-access model)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP with mysqli/PDO (include/lib/mysqlii.php, include/lib/databasepdo.php), installed via install.php
O10_build.project_tests: unknown; no test suite was found for loginauth or user_model during the screen

j.j_sites_touched: include/model/user_model.php (include/lib/option.php is a version bump only)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: addslashes/escape the username inside validateAuthCookie only, leaving the model function raw for other callers (or double-escaping the login path).
